findings.reason: the endpoint has to name the rubric in the key, or the section's guard refuses a review the system dispatches by design.
findings.text: s49's endpoint, "exactly one review run is created for each (node, head)", is narrower than the rule the section exists to make atomic: `_review_in_flight` is keyed on run, head AND rubric (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:961-1024, `_review_dispatch_field` at :240), and one delivered run whose commit changes a figure is dispatched a text review and a figure review for the same head in one pass (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:4195-4220). A worker implementing this endpoint as written makes the two rubric reviews mutually exclusive, so the figure review is either refused or never dispatched, and the done-when's "exactly one review run directory" is unobtainable for any figure-bearing delivery

findings.reason: without the followup naming s49 with the remaining implementable sections and dropping s45, the section enters no build invocation and the defect it measures stays open.
findings.text: f-qwnw-009, the plan's only open followup, prompts `/reckon-build queued-work-needs-no-workaround §43 §44 §45 §46 §47 §48` while the declarations at plan.html:23 read `s45: done` and `s49: implementable`, so a coordinator following the newest followup builds a finished section and never dispatches s49, the section this review was convened on

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py` resolves at the reviewed revision; the test file and evidence fragment are deliverables this section creates, not citations to existing files, and the cited `_review_in_flight` behaviour matches that module (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:961).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s49's done-when (plan.html:450) asserts "Exactly one review run directory and one review pointer result", which cannot hold for a delivered run whose commit changes a figure, because dispatch composes a text review and a figure review for one (node, head) (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:4195-4220).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — s49 writes its receipt to `docs/evidence/fragments/queued-work-needs-no-workaround/s49.html` under the repository, and its test to `tests/`, neither a scratch nor a node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — s49 carries no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags into the file it names, and its prose states the mechanism rather than a changelog.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — s49's endpoint is keyed on (node, head) alone, but the in-flight rule it means to tighten is keyed on (run, head, rubric), and the system legitimately runs two reviews for one head when the head changes a figure.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s49 names one deliverable, one review run per delivered head, with the crash case and the concurrency case as the two arms of that one measure.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — f-qwnw-009, the plan's only open followup (plan.html:502), queues `/reckon-build queued-work-needs-no-workaround §43 §44 §45 §46 §47 §48`, which includes s45 that the same document declares `done` (plan.html:23) and omits s49, which it declares `implementable`.
